reason: Both conversations reach the same honest, appropriately uncertain diagnosis (mains suppression filter vs control board PSU) and both route to an engineer without pushing a part purchase. Conversation 2 covers the expected next steps more completely, notably flagging warranty/Candy-Haier service and asking for the model number, which Conversation 1 omits entirely, and its extra safe checks (spur switch, cable inspection, burning smell) are sensible. Conversation 2's weaknesses are the softer 'don't open unless confident with electrics' wording and putting a home-insurance surge claim ahead of the warranty check, which edges toward an unsupported direction, whereas Conversation 1 holds a cleaner 'keep it unplugged, engineer only' boundary. On balance the more complete escalation and warranty advice in Conversation 2 slightly outweighs its mild hedging lapses.
